1.title: Hunting in Sentinel: Queries, KQL Jobs, Summary Rules, Notebooks and the MCP Server
1.text: Welcome to Module eighteen: Hunting in Sentinel: Queries, K Q L Jobs, Summary Rules, Notebooks and the M C P Server. It covers the exam area three. Perform threat hunting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Create and monitor hunting queries. Create and manage K Q L jobs in Data lake. Create and manage Summary rule tables for querying. Hunt for threats by using Notebooks, including connection to the Sentinel M C P Server. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three. Perform threat hunting (twenty to twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: The Sentinel Hunting page
1.text: The Sentinel Hunting page. Path in the Defender portal: Microsoft Sentinel, then Threat management, then Hunting. Tabs: Queries, Bookmarks, Hunts (preview).

1.title: The Sentinel Hunting page, continued
1.text: The Sentinel Hunting page. The figure shows this: Hunting queries, K Q L jobs, summary rules and notebooks each fit a different job.

1.title: The Sentinel Hunting page, continued
1.text: The Sentinel Hunting page. Queries tab. Content hub and custom queries, grouped by my ter attack tactic and technique. Run. Run all queries, Run selected queries, or a single query. Results delta. Compares the last twenty-four hours with the previous twenty-four to forty-eight hours. Favorites. Run automatically each time the Hunting page opens. N or A. The query lacks required data sources (hover to see them). Create an alert. From query results: New alert rule, then Create Microsoft Sentinel alert. Livestream. No longer available; use K Q L jobs, analytics rules or playbooks.

1.title: The Sentinel Hunting page, continued
1.text: The Sentinel Hunting page. Create. Only in the Azure portal; in the Defender portal you can view existing bookmarks. Fields. Name, tags, notes, my ter tactics and techniques, entity mapping. Entity mapping. At least one is needed to open the investigation graph. Storage. Hunting Bookmark table. Use. Add to an incident or create a new one; bookmarks are not in Advanced hunting. Hunts (preview) organize a hypothesis, its queries, bookmarks, entities and comments. They need Microsoft Sentinel Contributor (or a role with Microsoft dot Security Insights slash hunts ). Hypotheses can come from the my ter map, recent hunting query results, Content hub solutions or your own idea. Exam tip: Bookmarks are created in the Azure portal only. Livestream is gone. Favorites run when the page opens.

1.title: KQL jobs in the data lake
1.text: K Q L jobs in the data lake. A K Q L job runs a query against the data lake once or on a schedule and writes the results to a table. It is how you promote lake data to the Analytics tier so that analytics rules can use it.

1.title: KQL jobs in the data lake, continued
1.text: K Q L jobs in the data lake. Path. Microsoft Sentinel, then Data lake exploration, then Jobs, then Create job (or from the K Q L query editor). Output table. New tables get the suffix underscore K Q L underscore C L in the Analytics tier; one output table per job. Schedule. By minute, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly; start at least thirty minutes after creation; end date or run indefinitely. Latency. New data can take up to fifteen minutes to be queryable; use a delay. Roles. Security operator, Security administrator or Global administrator. Name. Unique per tenant, up to two hundred fifty-six characters, no or -.

1.title: KQL jobs in the data lake, continued
1.text: K Q L jobs in the data lake. Concurrent jobs. five (extra runs are rejected, not queued). Job timeout. one hour. Enabled jobs. one hundred. Time range. Up to twelve years. Not supported. adx(), arg(), externaldata(), ingestion time(), user-defined functions. K Q L queries in the lake (Data lake exploration, then K Q L queries) allow interactive queries with limits: five hundred thousand rows or sixty-four megabytes for a synchronous run, thirty queries per minute per tenant, ten concurrent; async queries time out after one hour and cache results for twenty-four hours; history is kept thirty days. Exam tip: Big, old, cheap data to query it in the lake. Need alerts on it to K Q L job to the Analytics tier.

1.title: Summary rules
1.text: Summary rules. Summary rules aggregate large, verbose data on a schedule into a small custom table, so queries and detections on the summary are fast and cheap. They live in the Log Analytics workspace (Settings, then Rules, then Summary rules, then Create).

1.title: Summary rules, continued
1.text: Summary rules. bin Size. twenty, thirty, sixty, one hundred twenty, one hundred eighty, three hundred sixty, seven hundred twenty or one thousand four hundred forty minutes. Destination table. Name must end in underscore C L. Query. Do not add a time filter; the bin size controls the time range. Source. Analytics tables (most operators), or one Basic table (with lookup to up to five Analytics tables). Target size. Results should be at most zero point zero one percent of the source; each record under one megabyte.

1.title: Summary rules, continued
1.text: Summary rules. Limits. one hundred active rules per workspace. Failures. Each failed bin retries up to ten times in eight hours; eight consecutive failures make the rule inactive. Monitoring. Table L A Summary Logs (Started, Succeeded, Failed). Roles. Log Analytics Contributor to create or change; Log Analytics Reader to query. Exam tip: Summary rule equals reduce volume (aggregate). K Q L job equals move or enrich lake data. Both write to a table with underscore C L or underscore K Q L underscore C L.

1.title: Notebooks in the data lake
1.text: Notebooks in the data lake. Notebooks run Python and Spark in Visual Studio Code with the Microsoft Sentinel extension, for deep hunting, machine learning and graph building. M S T I C pie, the open-source Microsoft threat intelligence library, helps in investigations.

1.title: Notebooks in the data lake, continued
1.text: Notebooks in the data lake. Provider. Class Microsoft Sentinel Provider from sentinel lake.providers, created with spark; methods read table and save as table. Pools. Small (light work, lower cost), Medium (E T L, joins, aggregations, M L training), Large (deep learning, heavy shuffles, time-sensitive). Session start. About three to five minutes; default session timeout thirty minutes. Limits. Interactive inactivity twenty minutes; notebook job eight hours; three concurrent notebook jobs; V S Code shows one hundred thousand rows. Libraries. Azure Synapse libraries three point four and the Sentinel provider only; no pip installs. Roles. Security operator, Security administrator, Global administrator to write.

2.title: The Microsoft Sentinel MCP server
2.text: The Microsoft Sentinel M C P server. The Model Context Protocol (M C P) server is a hosted service that lets A I tools and agents query Sentinel data with the user's own permissions. It uses Microsoft Entra for identity; there is no infrastructure to deploy. Data exploration. Search tables, query the lake, analyze entities. Triage. Triage incidents and hunt over your data. Security Copilot agent creation. Create Security Copilot agents.

2.title: The Microsoft Sentinel MCP server, continued
2.text: The Microsoft Sentinel M C P server. Prerequisite. Most tools need data lake onboarding. Role. Security reader is needed to list and invoke tools. Clients. Security Copilot, Copilot Studio, Foundry, Visual Studio Code. Custom tools. Build an M C P tool from a saved K Q L query in advanced hunting. Exam tip: M C P is how an A I client reaches Sentinel data. It cannot see more than the signed-in user's permissions allow.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Verbose firewall logs are very large. The sock wants an hourly summary in a small table for fast detection queries. What should be created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A summary rule with a sixty minute bin and a underscore C L destination. A summary rule aggregates data on a schedule into a custom underscore C L table; bin sizes include sixty minutes.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Two years of network logs sit in the data lake. The sock wants a nightly job that finds suspicious connections and writes them to the Analytics tier for alerting. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A scheduled K Q L job with a daily schedule. A scheduled K Q L job queries the lake and writes results ( underscore K Q L underscore C L) to the Analytics tier.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A tenant already runs five K Q L jobs and a sixth starts. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The sixth job is rejected because the limit is five. Five concurrent jobs are allowed per tenant, and extra runs are rejected, not queued.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. An analyst wants to save interesting query rows for an incident. In which portal can bookmarks be created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Only the Azure portal; the Defender portal views them. Bookmarks are created in the Azure portal only; the Defender portal can show existing ones.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A data scientist trains a deep learning model in a Sentinel notebook. Which pool fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Large, for deep learning and heavy shuffles. Large pools are for deep learning, heavy shuffles and time-sensitive jobs.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A team wants an A I assistant to triage incidents using Sentinel data under the signed-in analyst's permissions. Which feature should be connected? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The Sentinel M C P server Triage collection. The M C P server Triage collection lets A I clients triage incidents with the user's permissions.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which suffix do K Q L job output tables get? Answer: underscore K Q L underscore C L. Question two. How many concurrent K Q L jobs per tenant? Answer: Five. Question three. Which bin sizes can summary rules use? Answer: twenty, thirty, sixty, one hundred twenty, one hundred eighty, three hundred sixty, seven hundred twenty or one thousand four hundred forty minutes.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Where do Sentinel notebooks run? Answer: Visual Studio Code with the Microsoft Sentinel extension. Question five. Which feature replaced Livestream? Answer: K Q L jobs, analytics rules and playbooks. Question six. Which M C P collection triages incidents? Answer: Triage.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Hunting page: queries by my ter, results delta, favorites; bookmarks created in the Azure portal only. K Q L jobs: lake to Analytics tier; underscore K Q L underscore C L; five concurrent, one hour timeout, one hundred enabled. Lake queries: five hundred thousand rows or sixty-four megabytes; thirty per minute; async one hour. Summary rules: aggregate; bin Size twenty to one thousand four hundred forty; underscore C L; no time filter. Notebooks: V S Code, Spark, Small or Medium or Large, no pip. M C P: data exploration, triage, agent creation; Entra permissions.
